text: The Patriots are in full crisis mode heading into Sunday's 1 PM ET matchup at Highmark Stadium against the Bills, with Drake Maye's early struggles—two interceptions and a lost fumble in last week's 35-6 loss to Jacksonville—now compounded by mounting injuries to the offensive line, as the team just placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve while signing rookie OL Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad to shore up depth. Maye insists Wednesday that his right shoulder is fine and isn't affecting his throwing ability, instead pointing to poor decision-making as the culprit for New England's 1-2 start and the offense's league-worst 9.7 points per game, while beat writers are openly questioning whether the Patriots are using their young quarterback correctly and whether Maye himself can turn things around after calling his own performance "unacceptable." With the infrastructure crumbling around him and the team's offensive philosophy apparently in question, Maye will need to execute a sharper gameplan this Sunday to avoid falling further behind in the AFC East.
